source_snapshot.items: Test BMC I2C-6 connectivity to Mezzanine Network Board2 IO expander and FRU
source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC bus5, run the literal `i2c detect -y -q 5`, read mux0x76, write0x02 for port1, then repeat detection; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic result/photo collection and unexpected-log checks; no address or register-level oracle is defined.

historical_reviews.deepseek: Misclassifies a functional BMC path test as physical-only and ignores broad-scan semantics.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly flags `i2c detect` versus `i2cdetect` and mux restoration, but preserves unsupported probing coverage and accepts discovery as sufficient support.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row127 Board1/mux0x72 is a completed baseline and cannot substitute for Board2/mux0x76; expected Board2 IO-expander and FRU addresses must be distinguished from upstream and unrelated bus5 devices.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Use a gated functional before/after path test, replacing ambiguous broad quick-write discovery with owner-approved address-specific reads when PID allows.

original_test_intent: Demonstrate that selecting mux0x76 port1 exposes the expected Mezzanine Network Board2 IO expander and FRU on BMC I2C-6, with device-specific replies and no unintended bus impact.
original_method: Map BMC I2C-6 to bus5 and PID1114953 Board2 topology; inventory expected upstream and port1 addresses; capture mux state/ownership; select0x02 only with approval; perform safe address-specific IO-expander identity/status and FRU signature/header reads; compare pre/post visibility; restore the exact mux byte and verify bus/BMC health.
manual_activity: The BMC/platform owner supplies the Board2 mux/endpoint map, approves safe per-address transactions and mux restoration, and reviews evidence. Physical probing/photos are not core coverage unless separately required.
required_inputs: Expected Board2 IO-expander address, safe identity/status register and value/mask
Expected FRU EEPROM address, safe read offset/length and immutable signature/checksum oracle
Installed i2c-tools command set and owner-approved replacement for literal `i2c detect -y -q 5`
Mux0x76 byte semantics, bus owner/exclusive window and original-state restoration
Timeout/NACK/error criteria plus independent BMC recovery
safety_requirements: Do not run an unresolved `i2c detect` spelling or broad quick-write scan
Do not probe arbitrary addresses; use only PID-approved non-mutating endpoint reads
Confirm no daemon/driver owns bus5 or mux0x76 before forced/raw access
Capture original mux byte and preserve any required channel bits rather than assuming0x02 replacement is harmless
Abort on unexpected address delta, NACK, arbitration loss, stuck bus, FRU/IO-expander anomaly or BMC degradation; restore exact state
agent_execution_scope: Validate Board2 identity/topology, installed tools, bus ownership and read-only pre-state
After approval, perform one bounded mux selection and exact endpoint reads followed by restoration
Do not probe/solder, run a blind quick-write scan, write IO-expander/FRU content, guess endpoints, leave mux changed, reset BMC or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Board2 endpoint/address/register oracle and safe read operations
Resolve source command spelling and whether broad discovery is prohibited/replaced
Approve mux write, exclusivity, aborts, restoration and recovery
Review Board2-specific visibility and content evidence and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect: it discards the explicit remote before/after bus procedure and invents physical probing.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not execute literal `i2c detect -y -q 5`. Resolve the supported tool and prefer PID-defined safe endpoint reads before/after approved `i2cget -f -y 5 0x76` plus `i2ctransfer -y 5 w1@0x76 0x02`; restore the recorded byte.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC bus5, mux0x76, port1/value0x02, Board2 IO expander/FRU, PID1114953, Common branch and 15/5-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Compare PID-approved IO-expander/FRU reads before and after controlled port1 selection, then restore routing.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces ambiguous/broad quick-write detection with exact safe endpoint evidence and rejects invented physical probing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A new address after mux selection is insufficient unless it is identified as the Board2 IO expander or FRU and returns the expected device-specific content.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Quick-write discovery can interact badly with some devices; mux replacement can hide other channels; functional identity reads do not measure electrical margin.

project_override_considerations: Under Wistron I2C policy this is BMC/platform-management scope. Controller, bus, mux, endpoint addresses, safe request semantics, expected replies and OOB recovery are mandatory.
expected_evidence: PID1114953 excerpt mapping bus5/mux0x76/port1 to Network Board2 IO expander and FRU
Board2 identity, BMC identity/tools version, bus owner and management-health baseline
Original mux byte and approved0x02 selection/readback interpretation
Pre/post exact endpoint matrix: address, safe register/offset, expected and observed IO-expander/FRU values/checksums, exit status and timestamp
Evidence no unrelated bus5 addresses/channels or BMC services regressed
Exact mux restoration/readback, endpoint health and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The literal `i2c detect` command is not established as a valid installed tool, `-q` discovery is not accompanied by an approved per-device safety contract, Criteria lacks expected Board2 addresses/content, and earlier reviews invent mandatory probing/soldering.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target path and functional approach are identifiable. Owner-provided endpoint map, safe reads and approval are normal RPUC prerequisites, so static review can continue.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row128 Wistron-HW Robust-00006-V004: provide PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-6/bus5 through mux0x76 port1 to Network Board2 IO-expander and FRU, exact expected addresses and safe identity/FRU read oracles; replace or explicitly approve the literal `i2c detect -y -q 5`, define0x02 bit-preservation, bus ownership/exclusivity, bounded error criteria, exact restoration and BMC recovery. Confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.

review_improvement: Restores the remote functional path test, distinguishes Board2 from Board1, detects the unsafe/ambiguous discovery command and requires device-specific replies instead of photos or address presence alone.
independent_technical_reasoning: This row provides a before/after mux-routing experiment, so it is not inherently manual. The meaningful signal is not merely that the scan changes: the newly reachable endpoints must match Network Board2's IO-expander identity and FRU content. Because the source uses an unresolved command spelling and quick-write mode, an agent should use only owner-approved address-specific reads; mux0x76 state and sibling channel health must be restored and verified.
